note: Prelude/.olean collision ratchet. Clean seeds a hand-rolled prelude and then imports Lean on top of it; .olean import is FIRST-REGISTERED-WINS (crates/clean-olean/src/import/load_register.rs:1309-1331), so every colliding name DISCARDS Lean's declaration and keeps Clean's. Where the types differ, tactics resolve a statement the user never wrote — the measured example being List.append_nil, which Clean states over bare List.append and Lean states as `as ++ []`, so `rw [List.append_nil]` on `l ++ []` matched nothing. Counts are flat-or-down. Do NOT raise a baseline to green a build: fix the prelude statement to agree with Lean, or stop seeding the stub (Environment::try_with_prelude_for_import). Measurement: crates/clean-olean/tests/prelude_collision_census.rs; artifact: data/prelude_collision_census.json; gate: scripts/check_prelude_collision_ratchet.py (wired into scripts/local_gate.sh). Established 2026-08-02 against Lean v4.30.0-rc2 `import Init`. 2026-08-09: retired the `Trans` family (411 -> 405). The prelude seeded a 3-universe, Prop-valued, outParam-less `Trans`; Lean's is 6-universe, Sort-valued, with `t : outParam (a -> c -> Sort w)`. Because import is first-registered-wins the stub shadowed Lean's class permanently, so `Trans.trans h1 h2` failed DIRECTLY (no calc) on Nat <=, mixed Nat </<=, List.Sublist and List.Perm, and `inferInstance` for a Trans instance failed. init_trans now registers Lean's exact spelling (plus Lean's `outParam` reducible identity), so `Trans`, `Trans.mk`, `Trans.rec`, `Trans.recOn`, `Trans.casesOn` and `Trans.trans` are type-EQUAL and no longer listed. `Trans.noConfusion`/`Trans.noConfusionType` REMAIN: Lean's noConfusion generator strips parameter wrappers (outParam/optParam/autoParam/semiOutParam) and Clean's does not, so the two differ only by a reducible identity and are definitionally equal. Fixing that means touching the shared noConfusion builder for every inductive with a wrapped parameter; it is left deliberately, tracked here. 2026-08-10: retired the wrapper decLe/decLt bare-spelled family (12 names: Float/UInt8/UInt16/UInt32/UInt64/USize × decLe/decLt). algebra_uint_dec_le_proof.rs (both the Nat-carrier and BitVec-carrier builders) now declares `<T>.decLe : (a b : <T>) -> Decidable (@LE.le.{0} <T> instLE<T> a b)` (resp. `LT.lt`/`instLT<T>`) — Lean's exact serialized spelling — instead of the bare `Decidable (<T>.le a b)`; the values are unchanged and still kernel-checked (the class form δ-unfolds through LE.le/instLE<T> to `<T>.le a b`, the same conversion instDecidable<T>Le already exercised). The 12 names are dropped from known_bare_spelled in this commit; baselines stay at 405/129 until the census is regenerated under a real `import Init` (CLEAN_PRELUDE_CENSUS_UPDATE=1), then run check_prelude_collision_ratchet.py --update to lock in the drop. Nat.decLe/Nat.decLt/Int.decLe/Int.decLt REMAIN listed: Lean serializes their binder domains mdata-wrapped, a separate spelling gap. 2026-09-28: the monad family became Lean's classes (docs/issues/2026-09-28-prelude-pure-proves-false.md): Pure.pure, Bind.bind, Bind.bindLeft, Bind.kleisliLeft/Right, MonadExcept.throw/tryCatch, OptionT.fail and StateT.pure/get/set/modifyGet are type-EQUAL to Lean now and leave the list (-12). Eleven new rows join it (+11, net 376 -> 375): Applicative/Monad rec/recOn/casesOn and MonadExcept.noConfusion/noConfusionType differ from Lean only in the shared recursor/noConfusion generators' binder info and parameter-wrapper stripping (the Trans.noConfusion case above); Except.instMonad, ExceptT.bindCont and StateT.instMonad differ because the default prelude's Except/StateT carriers are single-universe. The census rows were patched for this change ONLY: a release regeneration of the merged tree measures 413 type-differing rows, and the 38 beyond this change's (Nat.*/UInt*.toNat_*/decide_eq_decide/instToStringProd and others) were added to the prelude by other lanes without regenerating the census; recording them is left to those lanes, never to a raised baseline. 2026-09-29: the census REGENERATED over main (release, real `import Init`, CLEAN_PRELUDE_CENSUS_UPDATE=1): prelude_constants 1979 -> 2114, colliding_names 1275 -> 1393, type_differing 375 -> 413, bare_spelled 118 -> 139. The +38 rows are exactly the ones the 2026-09-28 entry above left to their lanes; none is new today, all were on main unrecorded, and the gate passed because it read an artifact nobody regenerated. They are RECORDED here, not fixed, and this is the only reason the baselines move. By family: (1) bare-spelled, stated over the bare function where Lean uses class notation, 21 rows -- Nat.div_le_self, Nat.ge_of_not_lt, Nat.le_add_left, Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right, Nat.le_of_not_lt, Nat.lt_of_mul_lt_mul_left, Nat.min_eq_left, Nat.min_eq_right, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (nat_floor_order_lemmas.rs, nat_floor_min_lemmas.rs, nat_totality_proof.rs; their module doc chooses explicit, prelude-ordered arguments ON PURPOSE, which Lean does not use either) and UInt{8,16,32,64}.toNat_div/toNat_lt/toNat_ofNat (uint_floor_tonat_lemmas.rs); (2) same printed statement, different binder info (Lean's are implicit / inst-implicit), 11 rows -- Nat.lt_trans, Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le, UInt{8,16,32,64}.le_iff_toNat_le and .lt_iff_toNat_lt, instToStringProd; (3) Lean's type carries an mdata wrapper, 4 rows -- Nat.toUInt{8,16,32,64}; (4) different head spelling, 2 rows -- Nat.min_def (Nat.min vs Min.min instMinNat, instDecidableNatLe vs Nat.decLe) and decide_eq_decide (decide vs Decidable.decide). Nat.shiftRight's row changed only by becoming a Definition (3809edf31). Making each statement agree with Lean's is the fix and is OPEN, lemma by lemma: it changes argument order and binder info that Clean-side proofs and callers rely on. HOW THEY GOT IN: the census's only cheap freshness lane checked the RECORDED rows, so a new prelude declaration was a collision nothing counted; it now also asserts the live prelude's constant count equals `totals.prelude_constants` (crates/clean-olean/tests/prelude_collision_census.rs, census_prelude_side_is_current), so the next unrecorded addition fails without a toolchain. 2026-09-30: the rows recorded above are FIXED where the census can see it -- type_differing 413 -> 383 (-30), bare_spelled 139 -> 118 (-21), and the baselines move by exactly that; the regenerated census adds no row (prelude_constants 2114 -> 2145, colliding_names 1393 -> 1424: the 31 new constants below collide with Lean's and every one is type-EQUAL). Each statement is now pinned Lean v4.30.0-rc2's (`#check` under pp.explicit/pp.universes; `repr` of the stored type for mdata). (1) The nine Nat floor lemmas and the UInt{8,16,32,64}.toNat_div/toNat_lt/toNat_ofNat are stated through Lean's notation -- `@LE.le Nat instLENat`, `@HMul.hMul ... (@instHMul Nat instMulNat)`, `@HDiv.hDiv ... (@instHDiv Nat Nat.instDiv)`, `@HMod.hMod ... (@instHMod Nat Nat.instMod)`, `@Min.min Nat instMinNat`, `Not`/`GE.ge`, the numeral `@OfNat.ofNat Nat 0 (instOfNatNat 0)`, the bound `2 ^ N` (not UIntN.size) -- with Lean's binders and argument order: `Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right {m} (n)`, `Nat.lt_of_mul_lt_mul_left {a b c} : a * b < a * c -> b < c`, `{a b}` on mod_eq_of_lt/min_eq_left/min_eq_right, `{n}` on toNat_ofNat. The constants those statements name and the prelude lacked -- the `Div`/`Mod` classes, `instHAdd`/`instHSub`/`instHMul`/`instHDiv`/`instHMod`, `Nat.instDiv`, `Nat.instMod`, `instDivUInt{8,16,32,64}`, `UInt{8,16,32,64}.instOfNat` -- are registered with Lean's types and values (crates/clean-kernel/src/env/lean_arith_bridges.rs) and NOT as resolver instances, so what `/` elaborates to is unchanged; the elaborator's B101 bridge seed now registers the kernel's `instHAdd`/`instHMul`/`instHSub` at its old priority instead of defining its own. (2) Nat.lt_trans, Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le and UInt{8,16,32,64}.le_iff_toNat_le/lt_iff_toNat_lt take implicit arguments as Lean's do; instToStringProd's result level is spelled `max v u`, Lean's spelling. (4) Nat.min_def states `Nat.decLe n m` over `Min.min`, decide_eq_decide states `Decidable.decide`. Every proof is unchanged and axiom-free; prelude callers pass arguments in Lean's order. Surface pins: crates/clean-elab/tests/lean_statement_fidelity_rows_e2e.rs, every declaration in it run through the pinned binary -- the Lean-style uses elaborate (12 of its first 20 FAILED at the base) and the old explicit calls are REFUSED as Lean refuses them (11 of its first 12 were ACCEPTED at the base). NINE ROWS STAY, and not because the prelude disagrees with Lean: (3) Nat.toUInt{8,16,32,64} and Nat.shiftRight now carry `mdata {borrowed := true}` on each Nat domain and UInt{8,16,32,64}.toNat_ofNat carries `mdata {noindex := true}` on its numeral -- exactly Lean's stored types -- but Clean's .olean reader decodes `Expr.mdata` WITHOUT its KVMap (`ParsedExpr::MData(inner)`) and both converters build an EMPTY map (crates/clean-olean/src/import/convert_expr.rs and convert_expr_direct.rs, BuildMData), so the census's Lean side is `mdata {} Nat` and cannot equal any faithful spelling. Writing an empty map into the prelude would close the rows by stating what the importer reads, not what Lean declares; decoding the KVMap is an importer change (the parser, both converters, and the recheck fingerprint, which hashes MData as a bare tag) and is OPEN there, outside this ratchet. Dropped from known_bare_spelled (no longer bare-spelled): Nat.div_le_self, Nat.ge_of_not_lt, Nat.le_add_left, Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right, Nat.le_of_not_lt, Nat.lt_of_mul_lt_mul_left, Nat.min_eq_left, Nat.min_eq_right, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt, UInt16.toNat_div, UInt16.toNat_lt, UInt16.toNat_ofNat, UInt32.toNat_div, UInt32.toNat_lt, UInt32.toNat_ofNat, UInt64.toNat_div, UInt64.toNat_lt, UInt64.toNat_ofNat, UInt8.toNat_div, UInt8.toNat_lt, UInt8.toNat_ofNat. 2026-10-01: the NINE mdata rows are FIXED at the root, in the importer -- type_differing 383 -> 374 (-9), bare_spelled unchanged at 118; the baseline moves by exactly that and no row is added. Both expression readers now carry Lean's KVMap (crates/clean-olean/src/region/mdata.rs) instead of an empty map, so the census's Lean side of Nat.toUInt{8,16,32,64} / Nat.shiftRight is `mdata {borrowed := true} Nat` and of UInt{8,16,32,64}.toNat_ofNat `mdata {noindex := true} ...`, equal to the prelude's statements. Bool / Nat<2^64 / String / Name values are carried exactly; Syntax, Nat>=2^64 and small Int (which clean_kernel's four-variant MDataValue cannot hold without breaking trust-ir's exhaustive proof-DAG codec and wire tags 0-3, a cross-repo wire version) are carried as a String under the reserved key `_clean_lean_mdata.<kind>.<key>`, an injective encoding; a Lean key already in that namespace, a heap Int, or an unknown DataValue constructor REFUSES the expression. MData is kernel-transparent, and measured so: the replay batteries (native_fold_canon_lean v4.30 5/5, v4.8.0 4/4, replay_forged_lanes 13/13, replay_forged_header_lanes 3/3) pass with the same results before and after, and every one of the 786 pre-existing clean-olean lib tests passes unchanged (one, which pinned the dropped payload as an incomplete field, is replaced). 2026-10-08: List.not_mem_nil is no longer BARE-SPELLED -- bare_spelled 118 -> 117, and that baseline moves by exactly that; type_differing stays 374. The prelude stated it over the raw inductive (`{α} (a : α) : ¬ List.Mem a []`) where Lean states `¬ a ∈ []`, i.e. `¬ @Membership.mem α (List α) (@List.instMembership α) [] a`; crates/clean-kernel/src/env/data_types_finset.rs (init_finset_mem_empty) now states that, with the proof unchanged (the reducible instance projects to the flip of List.Mem, so the two are definitionally equal). It mattered beyond import: simp matches syntactically, so the raw statement could never rewrite a surface `c ∈ []` (trust-ir gap G25, ledger class (94), crates/clean-elab/tests/simp_list_membership_e2e.rs pins the stored head). The row STAYS type-differing on binder info alone (its printed prelude and Lean types are now identical): v4.30.0-rc2 binds `{a : α}` implicitly, while Lean 4.8.0 -- the oracle of the trust-ir program this change serves -- binds `(a : α)` explicitly (pinned: `#check @List.not_mem_nil` under pp.explicit on both toolchains), and the prelude keeps 4.8.0's, so `List.not_mem_nil a` elaborates as 4.8.0 elaborates it. Measured by census_matches_real_lean_olean (release, live `import Init`) before the row was re-recorded: totals 374 type-differing / 117 bare-spelled.
